notes: Added 24-Aug-2026 in response to a request to add 4 new money changers, whose URLs as given were all pages on klmoneyexchange.com — a THIRD-PARTY rate-comparison/aggregator site ('Compare live exchange rates from 7 KL money changers'), not any of those 4 businesses' own website. Building an adapter against that aggregator and labeling its output as e.g. 'Wawasan Ilham's live rate' would have violated this project's own Core Principle ('Do NOT rely on... Third-party exchange-rate summaries') and Section 25 ('Never silently substitute an alternative source and label it as the original money changer's live rate') — so it was not done. Instead, each of the 4 requested businesses' OWN official domain was investigated for a compliant equivalent (see README.md's Compliance section for the other 3 outcomes: Wawasan Ilham inconclusive/not added, Jags Money and KL Remit Exchange excluded). Jalinan Duta's own site (this file) is the one that checked out: real, plausible current rate data for CNY and 9 other currencies was directly observed in the page's initial HTTP response (a text-extraction fetch, not a raw-HTML/DOM capture — see 'verificationLimitation' below) on 24-Aug-2026, matching this project's existing CURRENCIES list (frontend/app.js) exactly in both magnitude and unit convention (e.g. THB/HKD/CNY quoted per 100, JPY/KRW per 1000, matching frontend/app.js's own CURRENCIES.base values with zero rescaling needed) — a strong signal this is genuine, current, correctly-scaled data rather than a stale or fabricated placeholder.
verificationLimitation: IMPORTANT — read before relying on this adapter or 'fixing' its selectors from memory. Unlike mymoneymaster.json/tajmuhabath.json/merchantradeasia.json, this config was NOT built from a raw HTML/DOM capture via a real browser session — the development environment this file was authored in has no outbound network access to jalinanduta.com at all (sandboxed egress allowlist), and no headless-browser tool was available for a live DOM inspection either. What WAS available: a text-extraction fetch of https://www.jalinanduta.com/, which rendered the rates table as a clean Markdown table with a 6-column header (Flag | Code | Currency | Unit | We Sell | We Buy) and real-looking numeric data for 10+ currencies. This is enough to be confident the DATA exists and is real, but NOT enough to know the exact HTML tag structure (table id/class, whether it's one <table> or several, whether flag images are real <td>s or CSS backgrounds) the way the other 3 adapters' selectors were confirmed. parseHtml() below is therefore written to be structure-agnostic rather than selector-exact: it reads the table's OWN header row to find which column is which (by header text: 'code', 'unit', 'we sell', 'we buy'), rather than hardcoding column positions or CSS classes that could not be verified. This is more resilient to being slightly wrong about exact markup, but it has genuinely never been run against the live site — the first real run (a developer's machine, or the GitHub Actions runner) is the actual first end-to-end confirmation, exactly as mymoneymaster.json's own notes describe for its own first live run. If it returns EXTRACTION_ERROR on that first run, that is the system correctly reporting 'SOURCE STRUCTURE MAY HAVE CHANGED' (project brief section 23) rather than a sign anything was rushed — inspect the real page's HTML at that point and adjust parseHtml() with actual selectors if the header-driven approach isn't enough.
requiresBrowserAutomationReason: The rates table's We Sell/We Buy values were present in the initial HTTP response of a fetch of https://www.jalinanduta.com/ (observed 24-Aug-2026) — no client-side JS execution appeared to be required to see the numbers, unlike Taj Muhabath or Wawasan Ilham's branch-select rate board (see README.md). A plain HTTP GET + HTML parser (cheerio) is the primary path, exactly as for My Money Master.
playwrightFallbackReason: Same reasoning as mymoneymaster.json: if this page ever moves to client-side-rendered rates, plain-fetch extraction fails validation cleanly (never silently stale) and this fallback re-uses the same header-driven parseHtml() against the rendered DOM of the same URL instead.
branchNotes: Jalinan Duta's own site navigation lists 3 separate branch pages (Bukit Bintang, Masjid India, Nu Sentral: /bukit-bintang/, /masjid-india/, /nu-sentral/), suggesting rates may genuinely differ by branch, similar to Taj Muhabath. However, only the homepage (liveRateUrl above) was actually observed to have real rate data during this build; the 3 branch subpages were not fetched or confirmed. Treating this as a single site-wide rate for now (branchSupport: false), same conservative default as My Money Master and Merchantrade Asia, rather than guessing branch-specific behavior that hasn't been checked. Revisit if per-branch rates are confirmed to differ.

primarySelector.description: A rates table somewhere on liveRateUrl, identified by ITS OWN header row rather than a fixed CSS selector (see verificationLimitation above for why). Header cells are matched case-insensitively, trimmed, against: 'code' (ISO currency code, e.g. 'USD'), 'unit' (the denomination the rate is quoted per, e.g. 100/1000/1000000), 'we sell' (the SELL rate — what the changer sells foreign currency to a customer for, in MYR), 'we buy' (the BUY rate — what the changer pays a customer for foreign currency, in MYR).
primarySelector.tableDiscovery: Iterate every <table> on the page; for each, read its first row's cells as the header. A table qualifies if its header contains a cell matching /code/i AND at least one of /we\s*sell/i or /sell/i. The first qualifying table is used.
primarySelector.columnMatch: Within the qualifying table's header row, record the 0-based index of the first cell matching each of: /^code$/i, /unit/i, /we\s*sell/i, /we\s*buy/i. Every subsequent row is a currency row; read its cell at the 'code' index (trimmed, uppercased) and compare against the requested currencyCode.

currencyDisplayNames.note: Not needed for this adapter — unlike My Money Master (which requires mapping an ISO code to a full display name like 'Chinese Renminbi' to find the right card), Jalinan Duta's table has the ISO code directly in its own 'Code' column, so parseHtml() matches on that directly with no indirection.

validation.notes: Ranges are sanity bounds only, set from the single live sample observed 24-Aug-2026 (see primarySelector.liveSampleObservedAt) with generous headroom — widen per-currency as real historical data accumulates, same approach as mymoneymaster.json. The site's own table also lists several rows that look like data-entry artifacts rather than real currencies (e.g. a second 'SARS' row duplicating 'SAR', and a 'SGDB' row with Unit 0) — parseHtml() only ever matches on the exact currencyCode requested, so these never get a chance to be selected, but they're a mild signal to treat this specific source's data with a bit of extra skepticism relative to the other 3.
